current_evidence: The council's 'How to apply for planning permission' page still links only this PDF ('Reviewed and updated on 17 October 2018'), a site-restricted search found no newer list, and the planning.data.gov.uk local-area-requirements record points to the same file.

issues.detail: List date is recorded as 2018-10-01 but the document text gives a specific day, 17 October 2018.

Grokbot captured roughly 25 requirements but the list has 41 local requirement headings. Missing: Accommodation Schedule (all development proposing new dwellings); BREEAM pre-construction assessment (non-residential 1,000 sq m+); CCTV details (any development proposing CCTV); Construction Logistics Plan (major, or significant construction traffic impact); Daylight/Sunlight Assessment (major, or potential adverse impact on daylight/sunlight); Delivery and Servicing Plan (major, or significant servicing impact); Economic Statement (major, or loss of employment site); Financial Viability Assessment (schemes not policy-compliant on affordable housing); Open Space Assessment (impact on open space, MOL, Green Belt); Parking Provision (new development, or development affecting parking); Parking Stress Surveys (major, or likely to cause on-street parking stress); Planning Statement incl. Secured by Design (major, or where policy justification is needed); Site Waste Management Plan (major or waste-related development); Statement of Community Involvement (encouraged for all majors); Sustainability Statement (non-major development not needing a full Energy Assessment); Telecommunications supplementary information (masts and base stations); Town Centre Uses/Retail Impact Assessment (main town centre uses outside centres, impact test over 2,500 sq m); Townscape/Landscape and Views Impact Assessment (most majors, protected views, conservation areas, listed buildings); Transport Assessment/Statement (major, or highway impact); Travel Plan (major development).
issues.evidence: e.g. 'Accommodation Schedule ... Application trigger: all development proposing new residential dwellings'; 'Transport Assessment ... Application trigger: Major development and other development which would have an impact on the highway'

issues.detail: Householder is recorded as '(none) ... national requirements only', but the PDF has a Householder Application Checklist that requires a Design and Access Statement where the site is in a Conservation Area and 100 sq m or more of floorspace is created. Several local requirements also apply to householder schemes: the FRA covers minor development, including householder extensions, in Flood Zones 2 and 3; the Heritage Statement covers works affecting heritage assets; and the Tree Survey covers works that could affect trees.
issues.evidence: Householder checklist: 'Design and Access Statement where the site is in a Conservation Area' and 'the floorspace created by the development is 100sq m or more'

issues.detail: All about 25 requirements are placed under Full planning with the note 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. Outline, reserved matters, change-of-use and s73 applications are all left as '(none)', even though most requirements are triggered by development type or threshold, not by application type. Examples: Accommodation Schedule (any new dwellings), Refuse storage (3+ units, including conversions and changes of use), Ventilation/Extraction (commercial cooking uses, typically change of use).
issues.evidence: Refuse: 'Application Trigger: proposals for new development, conversions or changes of use ... resulting in a total of three or more residential units'

issues.detail: 'Contaminated Land / Land Contamination Assessment' is placed under 'Minerals & waste (county)', and its trigger excerpt is actually the Landfill Statement text. Bexley is a London borough, not a county. In the source, Land Contamination applies to development on potentially contaminated land, especially sensitive uses such as housing and schools, and Landfill Statement is a separate requirement.
issues.evidence: Excerpt: '...Landfill Statements Required if proposal includes landfill proposals or likely to affect satiability...'

issues.detail: 'Structural Survey' is placed under Listed building consent, but the source's 'Demolition Methodology and Structural Survey' applies to any proposal that justifies whole or partial demolition (barn conversions, façade retention, basements), not specifically LBC.
issues.evidence: 'A demolition methodology and structural survey may be required in support of an application if the proposal seeks to justify the demolition...'

issues.detail: Several trigger excerpts are fragments copied from the wrong section. Drainage Strategy/SuDS shows 'treatments and SUDs, where relevant;' (from the landscaping text); the real trigger is all major applications plus non-householder applications adding buildings or hard surfaces. Waste/Refuse shows 'bicycles and refuse storage areas, boundary treatments and SUDs' instead of the 3+ residential units, HMO and commercial trigger. Highways shows 'public highway, visibility splays, landscaping...'. Sequential Test shows the fragment "Areas' then a sequential test may not be required." Roof plan shows 'and proposed Roof Plans, where necessary.'
issues.evidence: SuDS: 'Application Trigger: All major applications. All non-householder applications where buildings or hard surfaces are proposed'

issues.detail: Some excerpts carry text from the previous section or describe content rather than the trigger. Archaeological Assessment starts with 'Planning for Air Quality (EPUK/IAQM)' and is cut off mid-word ('applic'). Environmental Statement starts with 'energy assessments)'. Flood Risk Assessment and Noise give report content instead of the thresholds. Health Impact Assessment says only 'a rapid or a full HIA may also be required' and leaves out the major-development trigger. Air Quality leaves out the major development in or next to an AQMA trigger.
issues.evidence: FRA: 'Application Trigger: Application for proposals of 1 hectare or greater in Flood Zone 1;...'; HIA: 'Major development which are likely to have a significant impact on the health and wellbeing'; Air quality: 'Major developments where the development is located in or adjacent to an Air Quality Management Area'

issues.detail: The 'Submission rules' tab items are process text and contact details rather than validation requirements: the hard-copy sets rule, the CD rule for majors, 'We can also accept applications on CDs ... or by email to developmentcontrol@bexley.gov.uk', the rule against file-transfer sites and USB pens, and the redaction of commercially sensitive information. The item 'Further guidance: and 116950.pdf Land Contamination Assessment...' is a garbled fragment mixing a guidance filename with the start of the Land Contamination section.
issues.evidence: Tab item: 'Further guidance: and 116950.pdf Land Contamination Assessment Applications may also need to be accompanied by...'

issues.detail: Several Full planning rows (Block plan/Site plan, Floor plans/Elevations, CIL form, Roof plan, Existing and proposed levels/sections) come from the generic national checklist text and are not local list items. Their excerpts are the same run-on list of drawings repeated each time.
issues.evidence: Excerpt repeated: 'Location Plan Block Plan Existing and proposed Floorplans Existing and proposed Elevations (including flank elevations) And, in certain circumstances...'

issues.detail: The current Bexley list is itself out of date. Its policy drivers cite the London Plan 2016, the Bexley Core Strategy and the UDP, which have been replaced by the London Plan 2021 and the Bexley Local Plan 2023, and it uses old use classes (A3/A4/A5). Grokbot flags 'Outdated (>2y)? Yes', which is correct, but users should know the policy references are superseded.
issues.evidence: e.g. 'Policy Driver: London Plan 8.2 and 8.3, Bexley Core Strategy CS13, CS17 and CS21'; Ventilation: 'all applications for uses within Classes A3, A4, and A5'

summary: Grokbot's link is the council's current (and only) list, dated 17 October 2018, not 1 October. The extraction misses about 20 of the 41 local requirements, marks Householder as having no local requirements despite a householder checklist, and has many garbled or misplaced trigger excerpts and process-text items.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
